package_info.package_versions: Various (13% of all npm packages, specific versions not listed)
package_info.why_malicious: A significant portion of npm packages were at risk due to maintainers using weak or leaked credentials, allowing attackers to hijack accounts and publish malicious code to legitimate packages. This could have enabled widespread supply chain attacks affecting both direct and transitive dependencies.

execution_context.file_location: npm account authentication (not in package code, but in account management)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker logs in to npm account using weak/leaked credentials and publishes a malicious update to the package.
malicious_snippets.code_language: N/A (attack vector is credential-based, not code-based)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At publish-time, the attacker authenticates using weak or leaked credentials, uploads a new malicious package version, which is then distributed to all downstream users and dependencies.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Publishing package updates via compromised accounts is a classic supply chain attack vector, especially when weak credentials are used.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects only legitimate maintainers to publish updates. Here, attackers can impersonate maintainers due to poor credential hygiene.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate maintainers publishing updates to their own packages.
key_indicators: Use of common or leaked passwords for npm accounts
Unusual publishing activity from new IPs or locations

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers npm account credentials via public leaks or brute-forces weak passwords.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains publish access to one or more npm packages.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious update to the compromised package(s).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to all users and projects depending on the package(s).

attack_chain.action: Malicious code propagates transitively through dependency chains, potentially reaching up to 52% of the npm ecosystem.
attack_chain.leads_to: Widespread supply chain compromise and potential downstream attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual or unexplained package updates from accounts with previously weak or leaked credentials
Sudden changes in package behavior or dependencies after a new publish
Publishing activity from new or suspicious IP addresses
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in package.json or main source files
Addition of new scripts or dependencies in updated package versions
network_indicators: Malicious package versions making outbound network requests to attacker-controlled domains
Unusual traffic patterns from build systems or developer machines after package update
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package updates from accounts with a history of weak or leaked credentials. Flag sudden or unexplained changes in package content, especially if accompanied by new dependencies or scripts. Correlate publishing activity with credential hygiene and alert on suspicious patterns. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect malicious behaviors in newly published package versions.
